name: Red sweep
description: White aircraft with a thin red cheatline from the nose along the bottom of the windows, widening aft and sweeping up behind the wing over the rear windows to the crown at the fin's root. 'AIR ALGÉRIE' in red italic capitals and the Arabic name in red above the forward windows, a small Algerian flag ahead of them. White fin with the red bird mark in a red-ringed oval; red engines with the mark in a white disc; red winglets.

sources.title: Air Algerie, 7T-VKE, Boeing 737-8D6 (CC BY-SA 2.0, Anna Zvereva)
sources.note: 737-800 7T-VKE on the runway at Istanbul, left side, level, 2018-09-28. Fitted to shapes/B738.json (doors pinned, within 6 px): the sweep's edges read column by column off the photo, both titles' ends and heights, the flag, the fin mark.

sources.title: 7T-VKE AIRCRAFT Boeing 737-8D6 (CC BY-SA 4.0, Sg1959)
sources.note: Left side at Frankfurt behind a fence, 2026-02-15: the same scheme still worn (titles, sweep, fin mark, red engine and winglet).

sources.title: Air Algérie Boeing 737-8D6(WL) 7T-VKE (CC BY 2.0, Tony Hisgett)
sources.note: 2014-06-09: the scheme then too; not measured.

areas.name: red cheatline from the nose, widening aft and sweeping up over the rear windows to the crown

titles.style: Red italic capitals, wide and heavy, above the windows from behind the forward door.
The Arabic name in red, a heavy slanted geometric Kufi-style lettering, after the Latin name above the windows, ending over the wing's leading edge.

logos.description: The Air Algérie mark: a stylised red bird (an arrowhead of two swept wings) inside a thin red oval ring, wider than tall, in the middle of the white fin.
Small Algerian flag (green and white halves, red crescent and star) just ahead of the Latin title.
The bird mark in red on a white disc on the forward cowl.

notes: Measured on 7T-VKE (737-800, left side, Istanbul, 2018-09-28) fitted to the 737-800 shape, and still worn on it in February 2026 (Frankfurt). The sweep's edges were read off the photo column by column (red against white) and converted with photo_trace probe: the cheatline is about 0.15 m deep behind the nose and 0.5 m under the windows by the wing, its top edge leaving the window line at x 0.59, running just under the crown from x 0.70 and reaching it at x 0.77; the lower edge rises from under the aft windows (x 0.67) to the crown at x 0.83, the fin's root; the fillet wears it. 'AIR ALGÉRIE' x 0.186-0.295, the Arabic x 0.31-0.485; the baseline reads 0.37 forward to 0.30 aft in this fit (a slight roll), drawn at the mean. The right side isn't in these photos: assumed the same, the Latin name forward. The belly isn't seen. Air Algérie's 737-700s, 737-600s and A330s wear the same scheme.
